Subject: Tandem MAP: Evaluation -> Reservation plan for Pioneer Health GPU pools

Alex —

Thanks again for taking the demo yesterday. As promised, I wanted to kick off a short mutual action plan (MAP) thread so we can align the evaluation milestones with a realistic reservation timeline for Dedicated/Private capacity. High level goals:

- Get a 2-week evaluation running with our staging cluster (shared) by early July.
- Confirm workload perf targets (p99 <= 220ms for inference, 6M tokens/day baseline).
- If targets hold, lock a Dedicated tranche and parallel-plan Private deployment options.

Key questions for you:
1) Do you have a procurement lead we should include (for SOW/PO lead times)?
2) Any constraints on on-prem (air-gap, approved vendors, KMS)?
3) Preferred timeline for canary -> production (weeks after sign)?

I’m looping in Marissa (solutions) and Priyom (sales ops) to propose sizing and lead-time hedges. I attached a draft MAP worksheet and a quick sizing model.

Next step: can we do a 30-min sync Thu 6/24 to walk the MAP and acceptance criteria?

Best,
Ben

Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Tandem MAP: Evaluation -> Reservation plan for Pioneer Health GPU pools

Perfect — thanks Alex and Dana. Thu 10am PT works.

Marissa/Priyom: adding you to surface a pragmatic sizing + lead-time hedge approach. High-level recommendation (staggered tranches):

1) Eval tranche (shared staging, no reserve): immediate — 2 weeks. Purpose: validate perf and regression tests, exercise KV/prefix cache behavior.
2) Canary tranche (small Dedicated pool, short-term reserve): reserve 2–4 H100s for 4–6 weeks to validate production plumbing under live traffic.
3) Production tranche (full Dedicated pool or Private): reserve the remaining capacity in 1–2 tranches depending on procurement velocity.

Lead time notes: Dedicated (Redwood-managed H100s) typical procurement to allocation: 8–12 weeks for first tranche depending on region and SKU. Private (VPC or on-prem) with customer-managed HW: plan 14–20 weeks from PO because of vendor approvals, on-site assembly, and KMS/HSM onboarding.

Marissa — can you draft a MAP-backed acceptance criteria list and a quick tranches sizing suggestion against the attached model? Priyom — can you flag any typical contract flex (credits, SLA ramp) used to make the canary tranche lower friction?

Best,
Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Li <alex@pioneerhealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jun 2027 08:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Tandem MAP: Evaluation -> Reservation plan for Pioneer Health GPU pools

Alex / Ben / Team —

Thanks for the context. I reviewed the sizing model and sketched three concrete tranche options in the attached spreadsheet:

Option A — Conservative (fastest to prod):
- Canary: 2 H100s (Dedicated) for 4 weeks
- Prod tranche: additional 6 H100s (Dedicated) after successful canary
- Estimated Dedicated lead time: 8–10 weeks for initial 2 H100s; additional capacity can often be slotted faster once committed
- Acceptance criteria: p95 latency < 180ms, successful KV cache hit rate >= 80% across gen requests, no sample regressions on eval set (10 canonical prompts)

Option B — Balanced (hedge across Dedicated + Private):
- Canary: 2 H100s (Dedicated) + staging private node for early KMS testing
- Prod tranche: 4 H100s Dedicated + on-prem slipstream (if procurement clears)
- Lead times: Dedicated 8–12 weeks; Private 14–20 weeks

Option C — Aggressive (large upfront reserve):
- Prod tranche: 10 H100s Dedicated (single tranche), longer PO but lower per-token cost

Operational asks for Pioneer:
- Provide a short list of 3 canonical prompts and 2 sample data files for eval (sanitized).
- Confirm compliance checklist items for Private (HSM vendor, allowed OEM list).

I attached a one-page MAP milestones list (in the workbook) with owners and target dates. Suggested meeting cadence: weekly 30-min check-ins during eval, then bi-weekly during tranche onboarding.

Ben/Priyom — notes on contractual flex: we typically offer a 30-day canary credit and an SLA ramp window that can be tied to tranche activation to reduce procurement risk. Priyom, feel free to edit the MAP xlsx for legal/finance inputs.

-Marissa

Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
Attachment: Pioneer_MAP_v1.xlsx (updated with tranche options)

All —

Quick procurement/ops items from my side:
- If Pioneer goes Dedicated, finance prefers a 6–9 month initial commit for pricing and allocation guarantees. We can structure a shorter initial term for the canary with the 30-day credit Marissa mentioned.
- PO to allocation cadence: once PO is issued, we target allocation in the published lead times; exceptions require a signed acceleration addendum.
- For Private: provide vendor approval forms (we'll prefill where possible), and allow 2-week window for our infra team to review KMS/HSM details once vendor info is provided.

Alex/Dana — can you confirm whether Pioneer would consider a staged commit (3+3 months) to smooth budget cycles? That option helps us secure initial slots faster.

Thanks,
Priyom
